newsitem.title: UK: RTZ says metal prices lower than fundamental.
newsitem.headline: RTZ says metal prices lower than fundamental.

text.p: RTZ-CRA said the current price of many metals is lower than fundamental factors would suggest.

"The current price levels of many metals appear to be more depressed than the fundamentals of supply, demand and stocks would suggest," Sir Derek Birkin chairman of RTZ, the group's British arm, said in the company's half-year results statement.
"Market sentiment has had a sharp adverse impact on metal prices in 1996," Birkin said.
He said confidence was shaken by Sumitomo's announcement in June of massive trading losses sustained in the copper market.
"Economic indicators point to a broadly based improvement in the second half of this year and stronger markets in 1997," Birkin added.
"On a longer-term view, we are confident about growth of demand, especially from the Asian region which now accounts for a significant share of global consumption of all metals and minerals."
Birkin said, "For RTZ-CRA, with production of our major products still increasing and with our strong financial position, the longer term holds considerable promise."
